title: Hotfix revert playbook (scratchpad)
content:
Context:
- Canary flip on 2026-03-09 14:42 UTC for v2026.03.09-rc3 (image: registry.redwood/foo-service:2026.03.09-rc3@sha256:9a7f)
content_notes: Observed regressions in downstream LLM request latency and a 3% 5xx spike in canary pods (only in eu-west-1). This is my scratchpad of commands, things tried, hypotheses, and a minimal revert checklist for fast mitigation.
raw_body:
Timeline (short):
- 2026-03-09 14:42: canary rollout started (k8s: 4 pods, 10% traffic)
- 2026-03-09 15:05: Canary metrics show p95 latency +160ms, 5xx rate 3% (baseline 0.2%)
- 2026-03-09 15:20: Increased errors correlated with model cache misses in logs (kv cache warmup?).
- 2026-03-09 15:35: Decided to halt further rollout; start investigation

Commands I ran (keep for audit):
- kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=foo-service -o wide
- kubectl -n prod logs foo-service-canary-1 --since=15m | grep -i "cache miss" -n
- helm --kube-context=prod rollback foo-service 12  # tried to rollback helm release to previous revision
- kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/foo-service --to-revision=42  # note: revision numbers mapped to old image tag
- docker pull registry.redwood/foo-service:2026.03.08-stable@sha256:bb33d
- gcloud compute scp ./local-debug.sh canary-debug:/tmp/ --zone=europe-west1-b
- curl -sS -X POST "https://observability.redwood/api/query" -d '{"q":"service:foo-service p95"}' | jq '.'

Errors/snippets I captured:
- 2026-03-09T15:03:24Z foo-service-canary-2 ERROR [cache] kv get failed: timeout after 2s
- 2026-03-09T15:04:00Z foo-service-canary-1 WARN  [inference] model load slow: 2.7s (expected < 400ms)
- 2026-03-09T15:10:11Z proxy    502 upstream connect error; connection timed out
- Observability trace: root span shows long wait on redis lookup (trace: https://observability.redwood/trace/abcd1234)
hypotheses: 1. New image introduced a subtle change to KV cache management causing higher miss/timeout rates under cold-start conditions.
2. Model binary alignment skew with quantized kernels in rc3 -> longer model load times, evicting caches and causing downstream timeouts.
3. Network flakiness in eu-west-1 hitting a specific endpoint used by the new image (external config service).
mitigation_attempts: Scaled canary pods from 4 -> 8 to see if warm cache helps (kubectl scale deploy/foo-service --replicas=8). Result: slight latency improvement but errors persisted.
Forced warmup via scripted warmers (curl to /health?warm=1) across canary pods — decreased some cold starts but did not eliminate 502s.
Tried helm rollback to previous revision, but CI artifact promotion had already removed that exact tag in registry (stale refs). Need to reference image by sha256 to be safe.
Applied temporary traffic-split to direct canary traffic to dedicated lower QPS (istio split) to reduce failure blast radius.
rollback_playbook_minimal: 1) Emergency communication: post to #infra-incident and @oncall (pinned message) with short summary + JIRA ID.

2) If canary 5xx > 1% or latency degrades beyond SLO, revert canary image to last-known-good by sha: kubectl set image deployment/foo-service foo-service=registry.redwood/foo-service:2026.03.08-stable@sha256:bb33d -n prod
3) If helm/rollout undo fails due to missing revision: kubectl set image as above + kubectl rollout restart deployment/foo-service -n prod
4) Monitor logs for 10 minutes; watch p95/p99, 5xx, and traces. If stable, incrementally promote back to 50% and then full traffic over 30m windows.
5) Create short postmortem note and include artifact verification step into CI (ensure immutable sha stored in release metadata).
safety_checks_before_revert: Confirm image sha exists in registry: crictl image list | grep 9a7f or use registry API
Check DB migrations (none expected for this release) - verify migration tags in release manifest
Ensure schema/tokens used by canary are valid and not rotated in last hour
Notify customer success if customer-impacting endpoints are affected (CS triage).
post_actions_todo: Add artifact immutability verification step to release pipeline (store sha in release artifact in S3)
Add a smoke test that validates model load time < 400ms for each canary image before promotion
Run a canary in eu-west-1 with throttled external config service to reproduce timing dependency
Write up short incident blameless notes and attach logs/traces to JIRA-RELEASE-4321
